evidence.summary: The t10 pure-polynomial probe was itself buggy: it compared the unscaled polynomial (~1) against 2^x without multiplying by the 2^integer scale, producing spurious rel errors up to 1023; it is inconclusive as a measure of the kernel's approximation error. However the decisive evidence is the t11 exhaustive kernel sweep: actual FP32 kernel output across all 33345 finite BF16 values in [-10,10] has max relative error 2.26e-7, well under 1e-6, so FP32 rounding plus truncation combined does not push any legal input over tolerance. This contradicts c2.

rationale: Truncation error of the degree-5 Taylor polynomial for 2^f at |f|=0.5 is roughly ln2^6/720 * 0.5^6 ≈ 2.4e-6 relative, above the 1e-6 tolerance; coefficients appear Taylor-style (0.693147 = ln2), not minimax-fitted.

scope_evidence.summary: Every finite BF16 value in [-10,10] is legal and every output element must satisfy abs(actual - 2**x) <= 1e-6 * 2**x, with a single verdict over the whole domain.

scope_rationale: The contract requires relative error <= 1e-6 for EVERY finite BF16 value in [-10,10], including values whose fraction after floor(x+0.5) reduction is near ±0.5 (e.g. x near k±0.5, which are legal BF16 values in-domain). A failure there directly violates the stated tolerance.
statement: The degree-5 polynomial approximating 2^fraction produces relative error exceeding 1e-6 for legal BF16 inputs whose reduced fraction is near ±0.5 (inputs near half-integers k+0.5 for k in [-10,9]), violating the per-element relative tolerance contract.

data.stdout: {"metric": "actual kernel FP32 output relative error vs FP64 exp2, exhaustive BF16 domain sweep", "n_values": 33345, "max_rel_err": 2.2569583833987986e-07, "max_err_at_x": 0.2451171875, "count_over_1e-6": 0, "tolerance": 1e-06, "argmax_x_bits": 15995}

evidence.summary: Exhaustive sweep of all 33345 finite BF16 values in [-10,10] through the actual kernel: max relative error vs FP64 exp2 is 2.26e-7 (at x=0.245, worst-case fraction region), zero elements exceed the 1e-6 tolerance. This directly contradicts c1's prediction of >1e-6 error near half-integers; the actual worst-case error with proper 2^integer scaling is ~4x under tolerance. (Note: the t10 pure-polynomial probe was buggy — it omitted the 2^integer scale factor, so its huge rel values are a probe artifact, not kernel evidence.)

rationale: The polynomial is evaluated with fp32 fused-free multiplies (enable_fp_fusion=False) and coefficients stored in fp32, adding ~a few ULPs (~2.4e-7 at most) of rounding per operation, potentially pushing borderline ~1e-6 cases over tolerance even if the pure polynomial is close to the boundary.

scope_evidence.summary: Tolerance is a fixed 1e-6 relative error per element across the entire legal domain, defined in real arithmetic on the exact stored input value.

scope_rationale: The contract defines tolerance against real-arithmetic 2**x on the exact stored value, so any intermediate FP32 rounding counts toward the error budget; if the polynomial truncation error is near 1e-6, additional FP32 rounding may push some legal in-domain BF16 inputs over the limit.
statement: FP32 rounding in the Horner evaluation chain (5 fp32 multiplies/adds plus the final scale*polynomial multiply) adds enough relative error that combined with polynomial truncation some legal BF16 inputs exceed the 1e-6 relative tolerance even where the pure polynomial error alone is just under 1e-6.
